reasons: No test file is shown for this script.
The assertions protect against reporting on a run that changed data.
The field count and reference list are hardcoded.

terms.meaning: The recorded decision for a value, such as unchanged and unresolved.
A web search result that points toward evidence but is not accepted as proof.
A check that stops the script with an error when a condition is false.
The markup language that web pages are written in.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Folder and imports
sections.what: Brings in the built-in file, path and assertion tools, and sets the folder where the evidence repair files are kept.
sections.why: Likely reason: setting the folder once keeps every file path consistent.
sections.watch_out: The folder path is relative to the script, so moving the script breaks the paths.

sections.name: load
sections.title: Loading and checking earlier reports
sections.what: Loads the committed and rerun reports, then checks that the rerun added nothing and that no project values changed.
sections.why: Likely reason: a rerun that changed data would mean the findings are not based on a stable result.
sections.watch_out: If the rerun file is out of date, the script stops instead of producing a report.

sections.name: references
sections.title: Mapping unresolved values to research
sections.what: Lists which research capture files apply to each unresolved project, so each value has its own research trail.
sections.why: Likely reason: reviewers need to see the exact research behind each unresolved value.
sections.watch_out: A project missing from this list stops the script, so a new unresolved value needs an entry here.

sections.name: esc
sections.title: Escaping text and listing sources
sections.what: Escapes text so it is safe to show in a web page. For each unresolved value it lists sources, marking search leads as not accepted and fetched publisher pages as reviewed but not accepted. It also checks that exactly two new links were added and writes the findings JSON.
sections.why: Escaping keeps stray characters from breaking the page, and the source labels make clear what was and was not accepted.
sections.watch_out: The investigated field count is typed in, so update it by hand if the research scope changes.

sections.name: groups
sections.title: Writing the HTML report
sections.what: Groups the findings by project and builds one table per project with sources and reasons, plus a table of the new links, then writes the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: a readable page is easier for reviewers than the JSON file.
sections.watch_out: The page wording is fixed in this file, so any change to the review policy must be made here as well. The template is cut off in this excerpt, so only its general layout is described.

summary: Builds a web report and a JSON findings file from the continued research on unresolved budget values, and it changes no project values.
purpose: It shows each unresolved value with the research leads and publisher pages reviewed for it, and states that none were accepted as evidence.
why: Likely reason: it gives reviewers a written record of what the research found and did not find.
how: It loads the committed and rerun reports and checks with assertions that the rerun added nothing and no project values changed. It maps each unresolved value to its research files, builds source lists, writes the findings JSON, then groups the findings by project into an HTML page.
inputs: JSON files in artifacts/api-server/data/evidence-repair: continued-committed.json, continued-rerun.json, and the research capture files named in the references table.
outputs: continued-research-findings.json and continued-report.html in artifacts/api-server/data/evidence-repair, and one console line.
risks: The count of 43 investigated fields is typed in and not calculated, so it can drift from the real count. The reference table is also hardcoded.
debug: If an assertion fails, the committed or rerun file shows changed values or added rows. If a missing research disposition error appears, add that project ID to the references table. If a file is not found, check the research capture is in the folder.
